messages:
mina: Pushing a cleaned-up version of the min/max + SLO slider row. Goal: make the SLO slider feel separate so users don't mistake it for the capacity slider. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc/slo-separated. Thoughts on visual separation and copy?

nate: Love the separation. Suggest a subtle divider and a muted label: 'SLO (target p95)'. Keep the capacity row bold. Also the SLO helper should say what the number means in lay terms, e.g., 'Lower p95 = fewer timeouts but higher cost.'

tara (Product): Warning: don't overcomplicate SLO language. Default should be '10s' for conversational apps. How about 'SLO target (p95 latency)' label? And we should surface the expected cost impact inline: '+$2/hr at 5s'.

leo (A11y): A11y notes: the two sliders are close visually; ensure they have distinct aria-labels. The SLO slider needs aria-live updates showing both the chosen p95 and the expected cost delta. Also color contrast for the muted label is low on 14px.

mina: Good catch. I'll darken the muted label and add clearer spacing. For the SLO helper placement: inline vs tooltip? I think inline concise copy then 'learn more' expands a doc panel.

nate: How about a small 'cost preview' chip next to the SLO slider that animates when you move the knob? Simple micro-interaction improves discoverability.

ui-bot (bot): Design preview available: https://preview.redwood.work/slo-separated (branch: slo-separated-row).

tara: One more ask: keyboard-only users should be able to tab to the SLO slider and then use arrows to nudge. Suggest step sizes: 0.5s arrow, 2s page.

leo: For screen readers, prefer aria-valuetext like 'SLO target p95: 5 seconds; estimated cost delta: plus $2 per hour'. Keep the live region polite.

mina: Action items: nate ensure different focus styles and aria labels; leo write the aria-valuetext examples; tara confirm default SLO and cost calc; I'll push updated frames and copy by EOD.
